primary_claim: The general (broadly) misaligned fine-tuning solution is consistently more stable and more efficient than a narrowly misaligned solution trained with KL regularization to preserve non-target-domain behavior, explaining why emergent misalignment is the fine-tuning-preferred outcome.

effect.metric: training loss (efficiency) and loss increase under perturbation (stability) for general vs narrow misalignment solutions
effect.value: general solution consistently achieves lower training loss even after norm-matching (more efficient), and its loss increases less under orthogonal noise perturbation at any given noise level (more stable), across steering vector, rank-1 LoRA, and rank-32 LoRA setups

contradicts_or_qualifies: Previous work (Soligo et al., Wang et al.) extracted the misalignment direction and showed it could be steered/ablated but did not explain why 'be generally evil' is a natural fine-tuning solution — this post offers a stability/efficiency-based mechanistic explanation
stated_future_work: Investigate why this general notion of evil emerges as a seemingly core and efficiently represented concept during pre-training
Investigate what behaviours fall into this common misalignment representation space and the implications for monitoring capabilities in training and deployment
limitations_stated: The top 3 principal components (79% variance) of the steering vector training trajectory are insufficient to replicate the misaligned behaviour, so cannot simply be labeled as narrow vs general misalignment directions
Training narrow misalignment via multi-epoch training on very few samples has limitations, including much lower rates of bad medical advice and sometimes producing misaligned responses in Mandarin
quote: The general misalignment solution is consistently more stable and more efficient than the narrow solution.
